chapters.name: Overview
chapters.title: An interface is a living system.
chapters.lead: Follow one saved ChatGPT interface from document shell and preloaded scripts to styled components, state management, and network-facing code. Every connection is bounded by what this snapshot actually captured.

sections.title: Begin with the visible document
sections.body: The captured page exposes semantic regions, controls, serialized route data, and resource hints. It is one authenticated browser state—not a complete site crawl.

sections.title: Follow the code that assembles it
sections.body: JavaScript bundles contain bootstrap, event, state, request, and media-related syntax. Candidate references show where to investigate; they are not proof of executed imports.

sections.title: See the uncertainty as part of the story
sections.body: Source-level observations and runtime verification occupy different evidence classes. Missing files, dynamic event ownership, and actual network responses remain open research boundaries.

chapters.unknown: A static ZIP cannot independently prove runtime call order, server-side implementation, or actual user interactions.

chapters.name: HTML
chapters.title: The document is the interface's skeleton.
chapters.lead: Landmarks, controls, links and stream placeholders reveal the rendered application structure before any assumptions about its runtime wiring.

sections.title: A measured navigation hierarchy
sections.body: Both navigation elements are inside side regions. Among 130 buttons, 70 belong to navigation as their closest semantic landmark and another 42 belong directly to the main region. This tells us about the saved document, not the source component tree.

sections.title: Semantic regions
sections.body: The source contains one main landmark, two navigation regions, two headers, two asides and a form. This is a particular conversation-facing DOM state.

sections.title: Bootstrap alongside markup
sections.body: Sixteen executable inline scripts and two JSON script elements appear in the document, along with one external script reference and 72 modulepreloads.

sections.title: Interactive affordances
sections.body: Buttons, a form and file inputs establish possible interactions, but source markup alone cannot assign live handlers or verify successful submission.

chapters.unknown: The snapshot does not enumerate hidden menus or other routes absent from this DOM.

chapters.name: CSS
chapters.title: A design language in thousands of declarations.
chapters.lead: Stylesheets reveal theme tokens, layout rules, container conditions, motion preferences and a layered visual vocabulary—without reproducing the site's proprietary CSS.

sections.title: Token families and responsive regimes
sections.body: The styles contain 2,509 distinct custom-property names grouped into color, typography, spacing and other families. Media, container and motion conditions form overlapping source-level regimes; no browser-computed styles were captured.

sections.title: How styles enter the page
sections.body: Eighteen stylesheet links resolve to seventeen saved CSS assets, with one asset referenced twice. Layer, media and container at-rules are present, but computed cascade order remains untested.

sections.title: Tokens before pixels
sections.body: 2,509 distinct custom-property names appear across 8,135 declarations, including color, type, shell and component families. Names and declarations are not the same count.

sections.title: Responsive conditions
sections.body: The styles contain width/hover/pointer rules, 269 width-container conditions and 258 style-container conditions. Conditions may overlap.

sections.title: Motion and accessibility
sections.body: Reduced-motion conditions, focus-visible selectors and view-transition syntax coexist in the stylesheet corpus. Rendered behavior is not established by source counts.

chapters.unknown: Computed styles, browser support and actual element-level cascade outcomes were not measured.

chapters.name: JavaScript
chapters.title: Bundles describe capabilities, not verified actions.
chapters.lead: The large source archive supplies the materials needed for meaningful module research. Its first map records candidate references and API syntax, not a validated import/call graph.

sections.title: Validated syntax, not simple filename sightings
sections.body: Offline syntax-tree parsing found 236 static import declarations resolving to captured resource ordinals across eight importing and 71 referenced scripts. These declarations are more concrete than textual filename matches but still do not prove runtime loading.

sections.title: Reference graph
sections.body: Ten saved bundles mention public asset basenames matching 71 other saved bundles, forming 300 candidate source-to-target pairs. String matches are not parsed imports.

sections.title: Boot and update
sections.body: Route-loader streams and React boundary helpers are evident in inline scripts; the larger bundles suggest deferred functionality and observer-based updates.

sections.title: Specialized pathways
sections.body: Worker, WebAssembly, WebRTC and browser media constructs appear as code signatures, without evidence of execution in this session.

chapters.unknown: Real dependency ownership and executed call paths require AST-level proof, source maps or runtime instrumentation.

chapters.name: Components
chapters.title: From document regions to reusable behavior.
chapters.lead: Rather than mistake every bundle or DOM element for a component, Viewsource separates observed structure from inferred component boundaries.

sections.title: Application shell
sections.body: Navigation, sidebars and main content form the observable layout. Their separation is a useful research hypothesis about rendering boundaries, not a recovered React component tree.

sections.title: Controls and state
sections.body: 130 button elements, popover state attributes and ARIA hooks suggest a rich interactive surface. The exact component props and owning handlers remain open tasks.

sections.title: Styled composition
sections.body: Generated CSS tokens, focus selectors and grid/flex rules can be organized by surface, provided that inferred ownership is labeled as inference.

chapters.unknown: The precise source component hierarchy and prop interfaces have not been recovered.

chapters.name: Logic
chapters.title: Actions change state; state can change the view.
chapters.lead: Event and observer signatures make the mechanism visible, while specific control-to-handler ownership remains unobservable from this capture.

sections.title: Events are abundant
sections.body: The saved code contains event listener registrations/removals and mutation, resize and intersection observers. Vendor code can account for repeated patterns.

sections.title: From input to effect
sections.body: A plausible path is input → handler → state update → render, but this diagram is explanatory, not a tested trace for any individual button.

sections.title: Media permissions
sections.body: User-media, display-media, peer connection and AudioContext constructors appear in source. Consent, activation and success remain unobserved.

chapters.unknown: No captured live event trace maps a specific DOM control to its owning JavaScript closure.

chapters.name: Flow
chapters.title: Read the page as a sequence of boundaries.
chapters.lead: The end-to-end model ties captured markup, preload declarations, styling, candidate client modules, and state/network mechanisms together without asserting runtime timing.

sections.title: Boot declarations lead to candidate modules
sections.body: The HTML references 72 modulepreloads and an external classic script, all matched to captured JavaScript resources. Syntax-tree imports help construct a candidate graph, not a verified execution timeline.

sections.title: Bootstrap
sections.body: The saved HTML carries route-related state, inline initialization scripts, and references to assets. Their presence is certain; chronological runtime execution is not.

sections.title: Presentation
sections.body: CSS layers, custom properties and responsive rules style application regions; JavaScript libraries may update those regions and control transient UI states.

sections.title: Data movement
sections.body: Fetch, streaming reader and WebSocket-related patterns identify network-facing implementation candidates, not observed server conversations.

chapters.unknown: No HAR, browser trace, server log or live timing profile was supplied.

chapters.name: State
chapters.title: Some state lives in the page; some survives it.
chapters.lead: The source includes browser persistence, serialization and messaging mechanisms. The values and user-specific keys are deliberately excluded from the research.

sections.title: Initial state
sections.body: The HTML includes serialized route/application data. This supports source-level initialization analysis but private values are never published.

sections.title: Persistence layers
sections.body: Local/session storage, IndexedDB and BroadcastChannel APIs occur in captured bundles. Actual stored data, ownership and expiry are unknown.

sections.title: State transitions
sections.body: Worker/message and browser event patterns suggest cross-component or cross-tab coordination, but no transaction history or live graph was captured.

chapters.unknown: This archive provides no reliable record of actual storage transactions or state-machine transitions.

chapters.name: Assets
chapters.title: Typography, icons, and media are infrastructure.
chapters.lead: Font tables and image structure reveal meaningful asset roles, while individual UI placements and download successes stay evidence-bounded.

sections.title: The icon sprite connects to the saved DOM
sections.body: Ninety-two SVG use references all resolve to the same captured vector sprite and to 23 unique symbol definitions. This direct resource-to-markup link is distinct from merely counting icon files.

sections.title: Typography families
sections.body: The captured files include OpenAI Sans Regular, Medium and Semibold, plus twelve KaTeX font families. Repeated formats do not imply different visual typefaces.

sections.title: Symbol systems
sections.body: One vector resource acts as a large sprite with 911 symbol definitions, separate from the inline SVG markup present in the HTML.

sections.title: Capture completeness
sections.body: The manifest reports 29 missing resource attempts: 17 HTTP 403, ten HTTP 404, and two timeouts. These are capture outcomes rather than proof of broken features.

chapters.unknown: Original assets are not redistributed; exact on-screen image use was not verified.

chapters.name: Evidence
chapters.title: Every claim needs an observation boundary.
chapters.lead: Browse original findings by evidence class and confidence, and distinguish completed static interpretation from live questions still awaiting defensible evidence.

sections.title: A stronger source-evidence tier
sections.body: The deeper phase adds a parsed import graph, semantic DOM nesting and resolved sprite references; it preserves prior weaker string-match graphs separately instead of treating them as equivalent.

sections.title: Observed
sections.body: Statements marked observed_static are grounded in captured bytes or derived structural counts. The label does not imply live functionality.

sections.title: Inferred
sections.body: Cross-cutting architectural explanations use conditional language and should identify which links are interpretations rather than direct observations.

sections.title: Still to establish
sections.body: Module ownership, live control behavior, request outcomes and security enforcement require evidence beyond a static ZIP or stronger parsing of the captured code.

chapters.unknown: Reviewed static findings must not be transformed into claims of verified live behavior.

chapters.name: Research queue
chapters.title: The work remains visible until it is earned.
chapters.lead: Every source-rich capture now generates a deeper research graph. This specimen has 57 materialized deep tasks with dependencies and separately tracked evidence-based completion; see which remain open.

sections.title: Source-rich captures launch deeper work
sections.body: Intake now adds a persistent second-phase task graph when a ZIP is sufficiently rich in files, scripts or CSS. Each task has a research contract and dependency list.

sections.title: Review is not automatic
sections.body: Deeper tasks are not closed by source-token counts alone. The first thirteen have specific structured evidence; the remaining investigations stay queued until supported.

sections.title: Story-first output
sections.body: The purpose of the analysis is to explain how a site's systems relate, not merely produce an ever-growing inventory of code tokens.

chapters.unknown: Queue creation is automatic; performing source analysis and reviewing publication remain substantive work.
